A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same standard-GP Bayesian optimization study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and rendered figures, support reliable comparison despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: v2 reports original optimization experiments over ten runs, surrogate-learning evaluations over five runs, and computational timing results.

after.justification: v3 reports original optimization, surrogate-learning and timing results, together with additional baseline comparisons and failure-mode experiments.

M1.justification: v3 adds SBO-1, which trains the standard GP using diffuse-prior MAP estimation with L-BFGS. The earlier ADAM/MLE GP-ARD and single-length-scale GP configurations remain as SBO-2 and SBO-3. The underlying GP/UCB optimization procedure is retained.

E1.justification: v3 removes NN-Prune, including its ResNet-152/Tiny ImageNet task, while retaining the six synthetic and five other real-world optimization benchmarks. Appendix B.1 newly reports a high-dimensional polynomial optimization rerun. Both versions actually evaluate ten main surrogate-learning tasks, despite v2's introduction claiming twelve.

E2.justification: v3 adds BNN Laplace and BNN HMC to the optimization comparisons in Figures 1-2. Surrogate-learning comparisons add Add-GP and report a generic Proj-GP instead of separately labelled ALEBO-10/20 columns. These substantially broaden the evaluated surrogate families.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce MAP/L-BFGS settings, BNN architecture selection through leave-one-out cross-validation, Thompson sampling with 3,000/10,000 candidates, and kernel evaluations across 50-300 dimensions using 500 training and 100 test examples. Original BO budgets and the main 300/100 surrogate sample sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained kernel-length-scale and MLE/NUTS comparisons, Appendix B systematically tests training optimizers and priors, EI and Thompson sampling, SE versus Matérn kernels, dimensional sensitivity, and UCB exploration strength. Figures 10-20 and Tables 8-9 provide substantial new evidence about failure conditions.

E5.justification: v3 Figure 8 adds standard-deviation reporting for optimization trajectories, including selected best, median and worst baselines. v2's corresponding trajectory figures show averages only. Ten-run optimization and five-run surrogate evaluations are retained; an increase in repeated runs is not established.

E6.justification: Surrogate-learning values are extensively revised: Mopta08 ARD-GP MSE changes from 0.048±0.015 in v2 Table 5 to 0.034±0.006 in v3 Table 4. Identical sampled data are not established, so this is a revised result rather than a demonstrated same-setting gain. v3 also adds MAP/BNN results and substantial prior, acquisition and kernel failure findings, while removing NN-Prune results.

T1.justification: Formal changes are limited to definitions: v3 explicitly specifies EI and SE in Equations 6-7, while v2 Appendix A.2's penalized NN-Prune objective is removed. The central GP/UCB equations and synthetic-function definitions remain equivalent. No theorem, proof or formal guarantee is added.

C1.justification: v3 qualifies the broad standard-GP endorsement by explicitly tying successful optimization to Matérn kernels and UCB. Its abstract and contribution list add diffuse-prior MAP training and failure modes under alternative settings. This materially narrows applicability and expands the central contribution beyond demonstrating strong performance.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds proposed explanations involving L-BFGS instability, restrictive priors, vanishing EI gradients, inadequate Thompson-sampling candidate coverage, and SE covariance becoming nearly diagonal. It also discusses log-EI and alternative SE priors as remedies. These substantially qualify v2's predominantly positive interpretation of standard GP performance.

D1.justification: v3 adds MAP tolerances and priors, BNN implementation and tuning details, TS sampling instructions, and disclosure that surrogate examples came from optimization trajectories. It removes NN-Prune details, explicit NUTS priors, and SVM/Mopta08 implementation provenance. A new ambiguity remains: Section 4.1 specifies Gamma(1.1, 0.05) for noise variance, whereas Figure 10 specifies Gamma(1.1, 0.5).

R1.justification: New references include Ament et al., Hvarfner et al., Li et al. on BNN surrogates, and Sobol, supporting the new experiments and discussion of earlier failures. Pruning-related references and Papenmeier et al. are removed. The principal additive, embedding and sparsity-based related-work taxonomy remains.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title and method terminology, revises the abstract, shortens the conclusion, promotes the original results subsections, and introduces a failure-modes section and appendix. Much of the introduction, GP background, related-work discussion and original experimental narrative remains closely matched.

P2.justification: v3 adds the settings-summary table and numerous ablation displays, redraws comparisons with additional methods, and presents SBO-3 separately with selected baselines. Existing tables and figures are resized or relocated, including the surrogate metrics and prediction-alignment plot. The document also adopts a substantially different template with wrapped tables and figures.

improvement.justification: v2's broad endorsement lacked systematic tests of common alternative settings. v3 Appendix B establishes important failure conditions, while the abstract and contribution statements qualify when standard BO succeeds. This substantially strengthens the paper's evidential support and practical guidance. Removing NN-Prune reduces coverage, and the inconsistent noise-prior specification weakens reproducibility locally, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the central gains.
